sentences.text:
The petitioner has filed the present criminal revision petition being aggrieved by the judgment dt. 12.08.2004 passed by the learned Additional Sessions Judge (FT)
No.1, Sirohi in Sessions Case No. 79/2004 whereby, the learned Judge acquitted the respondents from offence under Section 498A, 304B, 176 & 201 IPC.
Briefly, the facts of the case are that the complainant petitioner lodged a report before the SHO,
Police Station, Mandar stating therein that marriage of his daughter Neeru took place with respondent no.1 Laxman Kumar on 28.02.2001 as per Hindu rites and sufficient dowry was given to the respondent according to his capacity.
It was stated that on 09.04.2004, her daughter [2024:RJ-JD:22229] (2 of 5) [CRLR-838/2004] who was having pregnancy of 3-4 months was killed by the respondent at Mandar.
On the basis of said report, FIR was registered and investigation commenced.
The police after due investigation, filed challan against the respondent no.1 for offence under Sections 304B, 498A, 201 and 176 IPC.
Thereafter, charges of the case were framed against the respondent no.1 for aforesaid offences.
The accused respondent no.1 denied the charges and claimed trial.

The prosecution in support of its case examined fourteen witnesses and various documents were exhibited.
The statement of accused respondent no.1 under Section 313 Cr.P.C. was recorded, who did not produce any witness in his defence.
After conclusion of trial, the trial court acquitted the respondent no.1 from the offence vide its judgment dated 12.08.2004.
Learned counsel for the petitioner argued that the Court below without going through the entire record and evidence acquitted the respondents.

It is submitted that the prosecution witnesses PW/3 Achala Ram, PW/7 Rajendra Kumar, PW/8 Arvind, PW/11 Pura Ram, PW/12 Natha Ram and PW/13 Visa Ram have stated that the deceased was subjected to cruelty before death.
However, the trial court acquitted the respondents on the basis of minor contradictions in the statement of the witnesses.
It is argued that the learned trial court ignored the evidence brought on record which resulted into erroneous acquittal of the accused respondent no.1.
Thus the judgment of the Court below is liable [2024:RJ-JD:22229] (3 of 5) [CRLR-838/2004] to be set aside and the matter may be remanded back to the trial court for passing fresh order.

Per contra, counsel for the respondent no.1 accused argued that the prosecution primarily relied upon the statement of witnesses whose statements did not inspire confidence and they being full of contradictions.

It is argued that the charge under Section 304B IPC cannot be sustained against the appellant owing to lack of convincing proof to establish that the deceased lady was harassed and humiliated in the matrimonial home on account of demand of dowry soon before her death.
Therefore, no interference is called for in the impugned judgment and the appeal is liable to be dismissed.
I have heard the counsels for the parties and gone through the material on record.

From the evidence on record so also finding arrived by the learned courts below, it appears that the accused respondent no.1 has been acquitted on the ground that the prosecution has failed to prove its case against the respondents for offence under Section 498A and 304B IPC inasmuch as the deceased herself consumed acid being annoyed with the fact that she was not taken to Deesa for check up having gynaec problem.
The trial court has rightly come to the conclusion that if the deceased had consumed liquor being frustrated, then respondent no.1 cannot be held responsible for the same.
In the opinion of this Court, the findings given by the trial Court are perfectly justified and there is no illegality in the judgment of acquittal by the trial Court.

[CRLR-838/2004] In the case of 'Mrinal Das & others v. The State of Tripura, :
2011(9) SCC 479,' decided on September 5, 2011, the Hon'ble Supreme Court, after looking into many earlier judgments, has laid down parameters, in which interference can be made in a judgment of acquittal, by observing as under:
"An order of acquittal is to be interfered with only when there are "compelling and substantial reasons", for doing so.

entities.text:
Mrinal Das & others v. The State of Tripura, :
2011(9) SCC 479
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: If the order is "clearly unreasonable", it is a compelling reason for interference.

When the trial Court has ignored the evidence or Achala Ram vs Laxman Kumar (2024:Rj-Jd:22229) on 15 May, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/15172746/
2 misread the material evidence or has ignored material documents like dying declaration/report of ballistic experts etc., the appellate court is competent to reverse the decision of the trial Court depending on the materials placed.

Similarly, in the case of State of Rajasthan v. Shera Ram alias Vishnu Dutta, reported (2012) 1 SCC 602,' the Hon'ble Supreme Court has observed as under:--
"A judgment of acquittal has the obvious consequence of granting freedom to the accused.

entities.text: State of Rajasthan v. Shera Ram alias Vishnu Dutta, reported (2012) 1 SCC 602
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: This Court has taken a consistent view that unless the judgment in appeal is contrary to evidence, palpably erroneous or a view which could not have been taken by the court of competent jurisdiction keeping in view the settled canons of criminal jurisprudence, this Court shall be reluctant to interfere with such judgment of acquittal."
There is a very thin but a fine distinction between an appeal/revision against conviction on the one hand and acquittal on the other.

The preponderance of judicial opinion is that there [2024:RJ-JD:22229] (5 of 5) [CRLR-838/2004] is no substantial difference between an appeal/revision against acquittal except that while dealing with an appeal/revision against acquittal the Court keeps in view the position that the presumption of innocence in favour of the accused has been fortified by his acquittal and if the view adopted by the trial Court is a reasonable one and the conclusion reached by it had grounds well set out on the materials on record, the acquittal may not be interfered with.
Learned counsel for the appellant has failed to show any error of law or on facts on the basis of which interference can be made by this Court in the judgment under challenge.
In the facts and circumstances of the case, the present revision petition has no substance and the same is hereby dismissed.
The record of the trial court be sent back forthwith.

(MANOJ KUMAR GARG),J 19-BJSH/-
